rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken quantifier for a large amount or for “much of” when the thing being measured is understood.

example.english: I drank much more water than usual.
example.traditional: 我飲咗好多水，比平時多。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jam2 zo2 hou2 do1 seoi2 bei2 ping4 si4 do1

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose Cantonese way to express a large amount of something.

example.english: I bought much more fruit than usual.
example.traditional: 我買咗比平時多好多水果。
example.jyutping: ngo5 maai5 zo2 bei2 ping4 si4 do1 hou2 do1 seoi2 gwo2

rows.note: Use this when pointing out, demonstrating, or comparing a specific quantity, as in “this much” or “that much.”

example.english: Why do you need this much money?
example.jyutping: nei5 jiu3 gam3 do1 cin2 zou6 mat1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for expressing a great degree, including positive statements and many negative ones such as 唔係好鍾意.

example.english: I like eating spicy food very much.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 laat6 je5

rows.note: Use this after a verb or adjective to emphasize a large difference in a comparative, as in 肥咗好多.

example.english: The weather has gotten much cooler lately.
example.jyutping: nei1 paai4 tin1 hei3 loeng4 zo2 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use this when “much” means often or frequently, especially in everyday questions about repeated behavior.

example.english: Do you forget your umbrella much?
example.jyutping: nei5 seng4 jat6 m4 gei3 dak1 daai3 ze1 gaa3

rows.note: Use this comparison pattern for saying that someone does not V to the same extent as A, as in “I do not like Wagner as much as Mozart.”

example.english: I don't like drinking as much as you do.
example.jyutping: ngo5 mou5 nei5 gam3 zung1 ji3 jam2 zau2
